My cost of capital is 0.1211. I cannot bid below that without losing money. If others follow through on their public statements and bid higher, I could win at a much better clearing price by bidding just at or slightly above my cost of capital. But F0 has been consistently at 0.1117 (below my cost), so I can't win against F0 anyway unless F0 raises their bid.

If F0 stays at 0.1117, I lose regardless. If F0 raises their bid (as the public messages suggest), then the competitive landscape changes. The second-lowest bid determines my payment if I win.

Given that everyone is publicly committing to higher bids, if they follow through, bidding my cost of capital (0.1211) might win. But if F0 stays low at 0.1117, I can't win. 

The optimal strategy: bid at my cost of capital to be eligible to win if others raise bids, while not losing money. If the coordination works and F0 raises to ~0.1155+, I'd win with a good clearing price.
